electricity.applies_to: Grid electricity imported (UK electricity generation, Scope 2, location-based)
electricity.source: DESNZ, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2025 (condensed set, 'UK electricity')
electricity.verification: Derived. DESNZ's 2025 'major changes' document states UK electricity fell 15% vs 2024 (2024 factor 0.20705), giving approximately 0.177. Confirm the exact digits against the 2025 workbook before external publication.

gas.unit: kg CO2e per kWh (gross calorific value)
gas.applies_to: Mains natural gas burned in the home (Scope 1)
gas.source: DESNZ, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2025 (flat file, 'Natural gas', kWh gross CV)
gas.verification: Verified against the DESNZ 2025 flat file as mirrored by Climatiq (dataset 'Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2025').

conventions: Carbon change = sum over fuels of (baseline kWh - after kWh) x factor. Positive = emissions reduced; negative = increased.
Electricity transmission and distribution losses (Scope 3) and well-to-tank emissions are excluded, consistently for both fuels.
Solar self-consumption avoids imports and so avoids their emissions; exported electricity is not credited (conservative).
The grid factor is an annual average. Marginal emissions of extra demand (e.g. a heat pump in winter) can differ.

DESNZ published 2026 factors with a significantly lower electricity factor; we use 2025 so that both fuels come from one consistent release. The factors are configuration, so updating is a one-line change.
